newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen following Dow until U.S. poll.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen following Dow until U.S. poll.

text.p: German shares were expected to hold back from any independent moves and track the U.S. market ahead of Tuesday's U.S. elections.
"We are currently completely dependent on Wall Street, we're following it up and down," said one trader.
Dealers said the DAX index of 30 leading shares was likely to stay in a narrow range between 2,665 and 2,685 points.

The IBIS DAX, which reflects day-long electronic trade in the DAX index, was down 0.72 points, or 0.03 percent, at 2,669.47, following the Dow Jones index as it fluctuated around its Friday closing level.
Although the U.S. election will be the week's main focus, a flurry of German data and company results was also likely to keep the market entertained.
DAX companies, Bayer AG and Commerzbank are due to release nine month results on Tuesday, followed by Hoechst on Wednesday and Daimler on Thursday.

Daimler shares, which were popular last week and the most heavily traded in IBIS dealings on Monday, continued to rise, gaining 60 pfennigs to 90.50 marks. Car maker Volkswagen was also stronger than the market trend.
Monday's main market-moving news was the confirmation over the weekend of the merger between British Telecommunications Plc and U.S firm MCI Communications.
German utility Viag AG, BT's partner in Germany, climbed over one percent, or 6.35 marks to 568.25 marks.

SGL Carbon shares fell after the company's third quarter operating profit came in slightly weaker than expected, up 4.4 percent on last year at 71 million marks. The stock was down two marks at 170.00 marks in IBIS dealings.
